articles.title: South Bow Q3 Profit Beats Estimates
articles.description: South Bow reported $99 million in normalized net profit - its version of net profit adjusted for special items - for the third quarter, down quarter-on-quarter and flat year-on-year as Keyston Pipeline throughput dropped.

articles.title: Wars May Spur Faster Electrification
articles.description: The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have prompted an increase in EV sales to avoid retail fuel inflation and gas demand destruction in favor of other power generation sources. With COP31 starting next week, some participants have signaled that faster electrification could become the focus of the event. “I would like to see a strong outcome on electrification in our presidency-led decision,” this year’s COP’s head of negotiations, Australian climate change minister Chris Bowen, told Bloomberg. articles.title: The U.S. Has $50 Billion for Nuclear Waste and Nowhere to Put It
articles.description: Finland and the United States are exemplifying two opposing approaches to managing the mounting problem of spent nuclear fuel. Finland is about to open the world’s first permanent nuclear waste disposal facility. The United States is stuck in a cycle of endless political turnover and resultant gridlock about how to address the more than 90,000 metric tons of spent fuel sitting in temporary facilities around the country, posing a mounting public health hazard and tax dollar sink. The Onkalo site (named after the Finnish for ‘cave’)…

articles.title: Egypt Eyes Billions in New Investment to Revive Oil and Gas Production
articles.description: The Egyptian government is doubling down on its plans to accelerate the development of its oil and gas resources. Egypt now aims to achieve a production capacity of 6.6 billion cubic feet per day by 2027, supported by increased drilling, new exploration incentives, and greater investment from international oil and gas majors. In October, the Egyptian Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources, Karim Badawi, met with Cypriot Energy Minister Michael Damianos, East Mediterranean Gas Forum Secretary-General Osama Mobarez and international oil and…

articles.title: Trump-Backed Trade Corridor Advances Despite Geopolitical Resistance
articles.description: Armenian officials have commenced design work for the TRIPP trade corridor, even though an operating agreement with the United States remains to be finalized. US and Armenian officials announced in January a preliminary agreement outlining the establishment of an entity, TRIPP Development, that would manage the corridor. The agreement sketched TRIPP Development’s ownership structure but left operational details to be settled at a later date. Since then, there has been lots of positive talk, but little action to get TRIPP Development up and…

articles.title: Survey Shows OPEC Output Neared Pre-War Levels
articles.description: OPEC's crude production rose toward pre-war levels last month as Saudi Arabia led a further recovery in Persian Gulf supplies, according to a Bloomberg survey.

articles.title: America’s Hydrogen Revolution Stalls Amid Funding Cuts and Weak Demand
articles.description: Just a few years ago, the United States was developing new hydrogen hubs to support energy diversification and help achieve a green transition. However, the development of these fuel hubs has not proceeded as expected, with several major projects stalling and political support faltering. The Biden administration showed broad support for hydrogen production, aiming to massively expand the sector and advance green hydrogen development. articles.title: Oil Posts Biggest Weekly Drop Since 2022
articles.description: Crude prices fluctuated as traders weighed Iran diplomacy, recovering Gulf exports and broader market weakness.

articles.title: UK Cabinet in Push to Approve Drilling at Rosebank
articles.description: UK cabinet ministers are lobbying Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh to approve drilling at the Rosebank oil and gas field in the North Sea.

articles.title: Wall Street’s “Energy Transition” Funds Are Packed With Natural Gas
articles.description: As we head into the United Nations’ 31st annual flagship climate conference (COP31), to be held next week in Antalya, Türkiye, greenwashing presents a large and growing problem in the private sector. As the tech sector’s greenhouse gas emissions explode against the backdrop of the artificial intelligence boom and the clean energy incentives dry up under the Trump administration, Big Tech and Wall Street alike are funding a boom in natural gas, all under the guise of funding the future of clean energy. “On Wall Street, the…

articles.title: USA Oil Stocks Drop by Almost 1MM Bpd Week on Week
articles.description: Commercial crude oil stocks, not including the SPR, came in at 409.760 million barrels on October 30, the EIA's latest weekly petroleum status report showed.

articles.title: Kyiv Hits 6th Russian Oil Plant in Week
articles.description: Ukraine struck a sixth Russian oil refinery in a week.

articles.title: Orsted Reaches Commercial Operation at Revolution Wind
articles.description: Orsted announced the start of commercial operation at the 704-megawatt Revolution Wind, a 50:50 partnership with GIP that was among several U.S. offshore wind projects threatened with cancelation by the Trump administration.

articles.title: America’s Nuclear Revival Is Running Into a Fuel Supply Wall
articles.description: The United States boasts the largest nuclear power production capacity in the world, but decades of insufficient funding and policy support is now posing an existential threat to the ageing sector. In the past decade, the United States has added just one new nuclear power plant to its fleet, while many more plants are drawing close to being decommissioned, at a time when clean, round-the-clock energy production has never been more needed. The Trump administration has been bullish about restoring the country’s nuclear energy sector to its…

articles.title: Oil Traders Want U.S. to Release Sanctioned Tankers as Freight Costs Soar
articles.description: Some of the world's biggest oil traders are asking Washington for permission to put sanctioned tankers back to work, as a global vessel shortage pushes oil transportation costs to extraordinary levels. Trafigura, Vitol, Mercuria and Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. are negotiating with U.S. officials for licenses to purchase or lease blacklisted oil tankers, Bloomberg reported Friday, citing people familiar with the discussions. The talks involve approximately 50 vessels currently under U.S. sanctions. Treasury officials are considering approvals on…

articles.title: Oil Market Arrives at 'Remarkable Destination'
articles.description: The oil market has arrived at a remarkable destination, analysts at J.P. Morgan said.

articles.title: Energy Reliability Is Becoming More Important Than Energy Politics
articles.description: For much of the past decade, energy debates often pitted fossil fuels against clean energy. Governments announced dates for phasing out technologies, investors tried to anticipate which industries would lose favor, and energy policy increasingly became entangled with political identity. The war with Iran has exposed the limitations of approaching energy policy that way. When supplies are disrupted and prices rise sharply, governments become much less interested in ideological consistency and much more interested in keeping fuel available,…

articles.title: U.S. Oil, Gas Drillers See Minor Uptick as Oil Prices Crash
articles.description: The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States rose slightly this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Friday, with the total rig count in the US rising to 604, up 56 from this same time last year. The number of active oil rigs rose by 1, to 463 during the latest reporting period, according to the data. This is 49 above this same time last year. articles.title: ONGC Posts Highest H1 Profit
articles.description: The Indian state-owned company reported around $3.46 billion in net income for the first half of its 2027 financial year, up 82 percent from the same six-month period of the prior year as high realized oil and gas prices offset lower production.

articles.title: ONGC Moves to Take Over Venezuelan Oilfields, Recover $500 Million
articles.description: India’s state-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corp. (ONGC) is negotiating to take over operations at two Venezuelan oil projects within six months, a move that could give it control over production and sales at fields where it is owed more than $500 million in dividends. The company's overseas arm, ONGC Videsh, is in advanced discussions with Venezuelan and U.S. authorities, finance chief Anupam Agarwal told analysts Friday. The company expects agreements to be finalized within three to six months. ONGC currently holds investments in the San Cristobal…

articles.title: Norway’s Oil and Gas Industry Faces a Major Decline Without New Discoveries
articles.description: For more than half a century, Norway’s oil and gas production has been underpinned by a handful of very large discoveries, the last of which, Wisting in the Barents Sea, was made more than a decade ago. Since then, exploration on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS) has increasingly focused on smaller finds close to existing infrastructure, allowing operators to bring new volumes online faster and at lower cost. While this approach has helped sustain production in the near term, it will not be enough to arrest the NCS’s projected decline…

IEA Sees 4,800 GW of New Renewables by 2031

articles.title: UK Launches Energy Independence Bill
articles.description: The UK government's new Energy Independence Bill passed a first reading in the House of Commons on November 4.
